They are small, sturdy animals that weigh between 30-60 lbs (14-27 kg) and stand about 2ft (0.6m) tall at the shoulder. Their main defensive weapon is their tusks, which are actually elongated canine teeth. They are straight, pointed and can grow to be 3 in (7.5 cm) long. Speedwise, they are pretty quick. Some estimate their top speed to be in the 35mph range but that is highly disputed. They are highly agile and can clear 4 foot fences with ease. Guess who isn't deterred by any of the above: the mountain lion. We went back to some of the darkest places in our story—the places where Clint’s brokenness once took him and where choices were made that eventually caused so much pain in our marriage. But we didn’t go back to relive the past. We went back to take back ground. We stood outside the strip clubs that once represented secrecy, bondage, betrayal, and brokenness…and we prayed. We prayed over the women inside. We prayed over the men walking through those doors. We prayed over marriages and families. And we thanked God for what He has restored in ours. There was a time when these places felt like they had power over our story. Even driving by them could carry the weight of what happened there. But they don’t get to define us anymore. Yesterday, we built a new memory in the very places that once held some of our darkest ones. A memory of redemption. A memory of freedom. A memory of a husband and wife standing there together—13 years into marriage—no longer haunted by what happened, but grateful for what God has rebuilt. Sometimes restoration looks like going back to the places that once held pain and realizing… they don’t own you anymore. Clint Webb The Whitest Kids U’ Know had that rare sketch-comedy energy where every idea felt like it probably started as someone saying, “No, wait, this might actually work.” Trevor Moore, Zach Cregger, Sam Brown, Timmy Williams, and Darren Trumeter made sketches that could be completely ridiculous, surprisingly sharp, or weirdly elaborate for something that seemed like it was built around one insane sentence. The show had that mid-2000s cable feeling where nothing was too polished, but the timing and commitment were always there. That’s what made it stick. A sketch could start with a simple premise, then keep escalating until it felt like everyone involved was trapped by the original joke and had no choice but to follow it to the end. They weren’t afraid to make something dumb, but the dumbness was usually smarter than it looked. It had the feeling of friends making each other laugh first, and the audience just happened to be invited in afterward. A perfect show for anyone who likes sketch comedy with a little chaos, a little bite, and at least one moment per episode where you wonder who had to approve it. #viral #reels #instagram #explore #instagood

Match the Hatch! 🎣🐣🪰🐞🪲🌉 The Rio Grande at John Dunn Bridge is part of some of the most rewarding stretches of trout water in the Southwest and one of the most technical. Wild browns, cutbows, and rainbows hold in deep pockets, big pools, and riffles carved through the gorge. Some are stocked, which is exactly why how you handle them matters. Catch and release, done right, keeps this fishery more wild for the future ♻️ Things are heating up heading into summer, but the river keeps weekends cool while the fish get more active! 😎 Knowing what’s hatching, how to read the water, and how to present a fly convincingly is what sets you up for some calculated good fortune. Because the only thing we don’t leave to luck is having fun! Eric at @ramblinflyfishing knows this river and pup Flora takes after his patience. This fisherman’s approach banks on studied techniques and mixing things up to keep fish guessing in all the right ways. We drifted nymphs last Wednesday. Some things you might notice: - Protective cages for rewilding native trees (invasive Russian olive was planted back in the 70s along the Rio Grande thought to be helpful erosion mitigation at the time…) - Where there are fisherman there are birdies, and activity is a great indicator of ecosystem health. Pictured are riparian dwelling Song Sparrow, American Robin and Mallard Duck. There were plenty of Violet Green Swallows and flycatchers galore (see outtakes in Story👆!) as well as usual suspects heard on the wind: Northern Yellow Warbler, Yellow Breasted Chat and even Piñon Jay, a special endemic species that is threatened by habitat loss and other factors. - We can’t help ourselves with the 🩶🪨 Whether you’ve held a rod before or not, or just enjoy being out in nature, a fishing outing never ceases to amaze! Just bring your curiosity, open eyes and ears, and positive thinking. The Rio will handle the rest, even when the cameras are watching! Average lesson on how to drive a manual with your dad 😂 Driving a manual car is all about coordination between your left foot, right foot, and your hand on the gear stick. Unlike an automatic, you control when the engine connects to the wheels using the clutch pedal. To start, press the clutch fully, shift into first gear, and slowly release the clutch until you feel the car begin to move. That moment, known as the bite point, is key. Add a little gas as you continue releasing the clutch, and the car will smoothly roll forward. Once you’re moving, shifting gears becomes a rhythm. As your speed increases, press the clutch, move into the next gear, then release the clutch while gently applying gas. Each gear matches a speed range, so learning when to shift comes naturally with practice. When slowing down, you reverse the process by braking, pressing the clutch, and shifting into a lower gear to stay in control of the car. At first, stalling or jerky movements are completely normal, and every driver goes through it. The key is patience and practicing smooth clutch control, especially at low speeds. With time, driving manual becomes second nature, giving you more control over the car and a stronger connection to the driving experience.

Many of them play at The Long Time, a sandlot baseball complex in East Austin, about a mile past the city limits, where residential developments dissolve into fields, farms, and rugged ranch land. It’s a sanctuary for easygoing games between players decked out in denim jerseys and stylish wool caps. Some wear Texas-sized belt buckles, and many of the uniforms are decorated with custom embellishments. Usually, copious cans of beer are consumed, and pet canines roam the dugout at liberty. Kids dart around playing tag, and spectators spread out on blankets. It’s a cocoon of good vibes that feels like an antidote to nonstop tech culture. It also just feels quintessentially off-kilter in a way only Austin can be. Some sandlot teams rise out of common interests; for example, all the musicians, filmmakers, writers, and artists on the Playboys. Others come out of businesses, such as Meanwhile Brewing and Lone Star Beer, which both have squads. The movement has even ensnared the attention of executives from major companies like Nike, Tecovas, Huckberry, and YETI, who all play on sandlot teams now. Big names like Jack White and Beto O’Rourke have even appeared in pop-up games. Often, these games feel like mini festivals, with vintage clothing vendors, hot dogs, drinks, and live music. You can see all that on display this Saturday, April 18 in Lockhart at the Wishing Well, the other prime spot for sandlot baseball in Central Texas. The event is part of Fusebox Festival, which may leave you wondering—“How is this connected to an art festival?” Just think of it this way: sports isn’t so different from theater. They both have players, costumes, spectacle, and are fundamentally about entertainment. During my field season, I encountered my first Northern king cobra (Ophiophagus hannah) with @rajath__nj and it was a dream come true. Did you know? King cobras are the longest venomous snake in the world. They are not true cobras (Naja spp.), though they have similar hooding threat displays. Unlike other snakes, king cobras are known to “growl” instead of hiss due to the low frequency of the noise emitted. King cobras are apex predators and will mainly feed on other snake species. After envenomating their prey, king cobras will swallow them whole. King cobras are very intelligent reptiles. They cause almost zero snake bite deaths per year and will typically avoid interaction with humans. These snakes play an important role in their ecosystems and in our lives. They keep other snake populations under control and their venom is utilized in medicinal research. As Hornell players began celebrating near the mound, assuming the game was over, the Palmyra-Macedon batter ran to first safely and baserunners continued advancing. With no out officially recorded, Palmyra-Macedon capitalized on the confusion, circling the bases to score both the tying and game-winning runs while Hornell was still celebrating. The sequence resulted in a rare “walk-off strikeout,” where a strikeout technically occurred but did not end the game due to the uncaught third strike. Scientists at Cortical Labs have trained lab-grown human brain cells to play the video game Doom. The system, called CL1, combines about 200,000 human neurons grown on a microchip to create a kind of biological computer. These neurons receive electrical signals from the game and respond with their own activity, gradually learning how to navigate the environment through feedback. It sounds like science fiction, but the goal goes far beyond gaming. Researchers believe systems like this could eventually help model neurological diseases, test drugs, and explore how intelligence emerges from biological networks. In earlier experiments the same setup learned to play Pong. Now it can handle the far more complex 3D environment of Doom. The neurons are still beginners at the game, but the technology behind it points toward a new hybrid field where biology and computing start to merge. The bigger question is where this leads. “The Christian faith is a religion of world conquest. Are the giants who confront us big enough to qualify as giants? And have we taught our sons what they are supposed to do when they grow up? Part of fulfilling the Great Commission involves climbing the beanstalk.” — Douglas Wilson, Future Men There is good reason for our long-standing literary tradition of giant-killing and dragon-slaying. These motifs are common in Christian writing because they are anchored in ancient, sacred Scripture. We were made to slay serpents and to cut giants down to size. God raises up Grendels as He raises up Beowulfs. He writes a dragon into the story, but never without a St. George to slay him. “Christians are a race of dragon-fighters. Our sons are born to this. Someone ought to tell them.” — Douglas Wilson, Future Men We need to tell our children these stories, not because we need them to believe in dragons and giants, but because we need them to believe in dragon-slayers and giant-killers. “Fairy tales do not give the child his first idea of bogey. What fairy tales give the child is his first clear idea of the possible defeat of bogey. The baby has known the dragon intimately ever since he had an imagination. What the fairy tale provides for him is a St. George to kill the dragon.” ― G.K. Chesterton, Tremendous Trifles Without the legends, we are left with just the dragons. We know the dragon from birth from within and without, but we have no hope of seeing either dethroned. Unless, we’re told the stories. Tyranny is understood intuitively; liberty is only learned through story-telling. “Dragon-lore is truer than therapy-speak.” — Douglas Wilson, Future Men Fairy tales have a firmer grasp on reality than Freud. If we don’t read the right kind of stories, we will lose our place and page. We won’t find truth within, but we can find it up a beanstalk. Lounging on a couch has nothing on Logres and if you only have an hour, spend your time with the Pendragon instead of with positive thinking. Therapy-speak is merely the orc-talk of the moderns.

🤔 A keyboard is an input device used to enter text, numbers, and commands into a computer or other electronic systems. It typically consists of a set of keys arranged in a specific layout, most commonly the QWERTY layout, which is named after the first six letters on the top letter row. When a key is pressed, it sends a signal to the device, allowing users to type documents, navigate software, and execute commands. Keyboards can be wired or wireless, and they come in many styles, including full-sized models with number pads and compact designs for portability. Beyond basic typing, keyboards often include special function keys that control system features such as volume, brightness, and media playback. Some keyboards are designed for specific purposes—mechanical keyboards offer precise tactile feedback for gamers and typists, while ergonomic keyboards are shaped to reduce strain during long periods of use. Whether used for work, communication, or entertainment, the keyboard remains one of the most essential tools for interacting with digital technology.

The Santa Clause was released on this day in 1994 🎅 The Santa Clause is one of those 90s holiday gems that somehow manages to feel both goofy and magical. Allen’s deadpan delivery and slow transformation from cynic to believer really carried the movie. It was his big-screen breakthrough after Home Improvement, and you can tell he’s having fun with it. In the holiday movie genre, it’s a legit classic. It’s funny, warm, and has that weird charm that makes it rewatchable every December. The box office agreed too — it was a hit, making around $190 million worldwide on a modest budget. It snagged a few Saturn and People’s Choice nominations, but its real reward is how beloved it became. The legacy’s huge: two sequels, a Disney+ revival, and endless TV airings. It’s basically part of the Christmas movie DNA now. Game 5 of the 1965 World Series, held on October 11 at Dodger Stadium, remains one of the most masterful pitching performances in baseball history. On the mound was Sandy Koufax, who threw a five-hit shutout, striking out 10 batters to give the Dodgers a 7–0 victory over the Minnesota Twins. Over the course of the series, Koufax delivered an astonishing workload - three starts and two complete-game shutouts - including a Game 7 shutout on two days’ rest, clinching the championship and earning him World Series MVP honors. The 1965 Series itself marked the first time the Twins franchise appeared in a World Series since relocating from Washington, D.C. The matchup showcased the Twins’ powerful lineup (including Zoilo Versalles and Harmon Killebrew) against the Dodgers’ unmatched pitching rotation led by Koufax, Don Drysdale, and Claude Osteen. This clip captures a glimpse of baseball in its rawest, golden-era form - black-and-white film, tight uniforms, and fans packed shoulder to shoulder as Koufax redefined what it meant to be a pitching legend. In May 1958, CIA pilot Allen Pope was shot down and captured during a covert bombing raid against the Indonesian Navy during the Indonesian Crisis. After learning that Pope was being held on house arrest at a jungle resort on the slopes of Mt. Merapi, and had freedom of movement outside, the CIA’s Technical Services Staff came up with a plan to air-drop an inflatable airplane to him, so he could rescue himself. The CIA turned to the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company, who had already been working to develop an inflatable rubber plane called the Inflatoplane, including single-seat and dual-seat designs. The single-seat model could be folded down to 44 cubic feet with a 40-hp engine and propeller strapped on top. There was also an onboard air compressor to maintain positive pressure during flight, even if the aircraft were punctured by several .30 caliber bullets. The Inflatoplanes had relatively low top speeds and range but were considered more than sufficient for the Pope rescue scenario. Inflatoplanes were designed to be filled with compressed air from a canister, but the CIA filled the fuselage with water-activated chemical pellets instead. Pope could simply pour water into the reservoir, which would react with the chemical pellets, filling the rubber fuselage with an inert gas. Pope could then fly himself to safety. The prototype was tested and determined to be functional, but the rescue operation was ultimately canceled for unknown reasons. Pope remained under house arrest until 1962, when he was released after diplomatic negotiations. But at least one report stated he was rescued by paramilitary operatives. Pope returned to service with the CIA afterwards as a pilot on covert missions. Years later when another mission offered the potential of using the inflatable airplane, CIA technicians pulled it from the warehouse only to discover that the rubber was dried up and cracked due to lack of maintenance. I’ve been holding onto this video since January 30th 2024 from when I broke my leg flying into a tree in Sedona… The embarrassment that still creeps in when I watch this video… the complacency I held onto months leading up to this incident. There were many factors that caused such a stupid accident to occur that changed my everyday life. From me rushing up to Sedona after a long and stressful work day, to me getting antsy and frustrated trying to find a solid launch spot. To being on a timer, as the sun kept creeping lower and lower. I knew I had to take a risk after finding this mediocre//below average launch, “a good Paramotor pilot can take off anywhere” my famous last words before I flew head on into a Cypress tree. There was many things I didn’t factor in for this launch. I was 5k ft of elevation, flying a 16m Gin Carve (spicy) on a miniplane top 80cc with a 130cm carbon fiber prop (which let me tell ya, this set up boosted more power than your average 80cc) however I didn’t factor in being almost 4k higher in elevation from my normal launch spot in phoenix. As I launched I had to run by a massive dirt pile, peeling around this while still full throttling committing to this launch. Right as my feet get picked up off the ground the light winds crabbed my canopy into the only tree to my left. If I was slightly to the right a bit more I would’ve probably barely cleared the brush maybe clipped a line on the tree I crashed into but would’ve not be nearly as big of an injury. This is where my complacency had kicked in… I have had multiple close calls while launching through tight gaps in parks and even slalom flying through cactus. In the moment I had a feeling I could get away with one more sketchy take off. But unfortunately you have to learn from your mistakes and own up to your consequences of taking the risk which we end up facing in these extreme airsports. I still get embarrassed watching this cause it was so preventable, but I’m here posting it for others to learn from my mistakes and slow down in life. Not everything needs to be a rush in life ✌️🙏

A deadly tornado that killed three people in Enderlin, North Dakota, on June 20 was a rare EF-5 storm, the National Weather Service (NWS) announced on October 5. The last known EF-5 tornado in the US was recorded in 2013. Video from Eric Schultz shows the massive tornado towering above houses and silos as a siren rings out. “I was looking to the northeast out my front door. I thought the lightning was extreme and the cloud like formation was very unique. I did not know the extent of the storm yet,” Schultz told Storyful. Though the NWS’s preliminary survey rated the tornado as an EF-3+ – the first in the area in 15 years – it was upgraded to an EF-5 on October 5. In the announcement, the NWS in Grand Forks said it had “conducted additional surveys and worked extensively with wind-damage experts” to further investigate the twister. They estimated the maximum wind speed at greater than 210 mph after examining a train derailment south of Enderlin in which one empty tanker car was “tossed about 475.7 feet (145 m).”
